implementation_notes: Scala's Option is documented as best treated as a collection: map, flatMap, filter, collect and for-comprehensions chain absent-aware steps, and getOrElse/fold close the 0..1 case. For the plural focus, collections' map/flatMap/collect traverse 0..n and a case-class copy performs the structure-preserving update, so the classic optic structure is replaced by ordinary standard-library idioms. Reach for Monocle only when the composed path itself becomes a shared, reusable value.
code_sketch:
val city: String = order.flatMap(o => o.customer.addressOption)
  .map(_.city).getOrElse("unknown")

// 0..n, structure preserving
val repriced = order.lines.flatMap(_.toOption)
  .map(l => l.copy(price = discount(l.price)))
pitfalls: Option.get and .head throw on empty; getOrElse, fold or a for-comprehension keep the path total.
Mapping an Option-returning function with map nests Option[Option[T]]; flatMap is the flattening step.
For-comprehensions desugar to flatMap/withFilter, and mixing Option with collections in one comprehension pulls in the option2Iterable conversion, silently changing the result type.

variants.name: Monocle Optional / Traversal optics
variants.idiom_name: Monocle Optional[S, A] / Traversal[S, A] with andThen composition
variants.implementation_notes: Monocle provides the classic structure directly: Optional[S, A] is a partial lens defined by getOption plus replace (getOrModify for polymorphic updates), and Traversal[S, A] generalizes it to 0..n targets; optics compose with andThen/composeLens and are applied with modify/set/getAll over immutable case classes. Choose it when the same nested path is updated from several places or when the path should be a first-class value; it adds a dependency and some type-level ceremony.
pitfalls: Hand-written optics must satisfy the Optional laws (getOptionSet, setGetOption) or composition silently misbehaves.
Combining Optionals that target the same element into a Traversal violates the traversal laws; Monocle documents this caveat for applyN.
The optics dependency must match the Scala version in use, and macro-based syntax needs the macro module on the classpath.
